A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MeepleLM study. Main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 207 held-out games, ablations, persona analyses, and a ten-participant blind A/B study, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and adds a human audit of 200 synthesized MDA reasoning chains.

M1.justification: The persona-discovery pipeline, MDA reconstruction and automated verification, Qwen3-8B backbone, LoRA training, objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The added human audit is post hoc validation, not a modification of the method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same board-game corpus, 207-game evaluation, five personas, and familiar/unfamiliar-game utility scenarios. The audit checks existing reasoning chains within this domain without establishing expanded dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: GPT-5.1, Gemini3-Pro, Qwen3-235B, Qwen3-8B, and the three ablation variants remain in the corresponding comparisons. Newly discussed engine-based playtesting methods are cited but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 and new Appendix E.4 add an audit protocol: three experienced players collectively assess 200 chains, 20 per game across ten familiar games, using the existing verifier criteria. Previously reported training and benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new human audit checks grounding, causal plausibility, and rating consistency of synthesized MDA chains beyond automated verification. Existing component ablations, temporal analysis, persona robustness analysis, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Section 5.4 newly reports binomial tests against a 0.5 win-rate null, excluding ties, and Cohen's h for the existing user-study metrics. Participant counts and the underlying study remain unchanged; additional trials are not reported.

E6.justification: v5 adds the 200/200 audit pass result and reports p < 0.001 with h = 0.69–1.03 for user-study metrics. Figure 5 corrects the Case I Advantage Gap from '+-998.25' to '+1.77', consistent with unchanged WD values of 2.52 and 0.75. Benchmark tables and user-study win rates are unchanged.

T1.justification: The conditional-generation formulation, cross-entropy objective in Equation 1, and metric definitions in Equations 2–3 are retained. No theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive mathematical definition is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim of a reliable playtester for general interactive systems with experience-grounded feedback. The introduction explicitly distinguishes the board-game instantiation from broader framework applicability. The principal dataset, method, and performance contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v5 interprets the audit as supporting pipeline reliability and explains its restriction to familiar games through cognitive burden and expert-recruitment constraints. It also newly characterizes user preference as statistically robust despite the small sample. Existing multimodality and persona-granularity limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E.4 documents audit allocation, annotator familiarity, and reuse of the automated verifier's criteria. Existing training hyperparameters, deployment details, prompts, and code/data access statements are unchanged; the hyperparameter subsection is simply renumbered E.5.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a previously absent, directly relevant research lineage of engine-based automated playtesting, covering MCTS, procedural personas, reinforcement learning, and LLM self-play through seven added references. MeepleLM is now explicitly positioned as a complementary approach to subjective experience assessment without executable engines.

P1.justification: The abstract ending and introduction's closing paragraph are revised, related work is locally expanded, and an audit subsection is inserted. Typographical and affiliation edits also appear, while the overall organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 3–5 are redrawn with larger labels; Figure 5 changes from horizontal to vertically stacked panels. Figures 4–5 are relocated beside each other below Table 2, and the audit page is rearranged. Existing figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v5 adds limited human validation of the reasoning pipeline, addresses an important omission in related work, moderates the abstract's scope, and corrects Figure 5's inconsistent annotation while improving plot readability. These are useful incremental gains. The audit covers only ten familiar games, and the new statistical summary does not explain treatment of repeated judgments from the same ten participants, limiting its additional assurance.
